transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 10:30 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Aureus Head of ML), Sara Nguyen (Aureus Data Eng), Tom Li (Aureus VP Ops)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to pick an open-model shortlist, define success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost), and agree on benchmarks + timelines. Customer emphasized bilingual support (EN/ES) and heavy domain-specific finance terminology. Discussed hosted vs dedicated considerations and security (VPC, KMS, SOC2).

Topics:
- POC goals & success criteria
- Workload sizing and expected QPS / concurrency
- Benchmark design and metrics (latency, rouge/emd-ish, hallucination checks)
- Model shortlist (open models) and tradeoffs (quality vs cost)
- Multilingual + finance-domain considerations
- Operational constraints: VPC, data retention, audit logs
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're Maya from Redwood, with Luis our SE, and I think we have Ravi, Sara and Tom from Aureus, is that right?
[00:07] Ravi: yep that's right, hey all.
[00:10] Luis: morning, quick agenda — pick models, define success criteria, sizing, bench plan. should be about 45.
[00:18] Tom: sounds good. we want to run a short 4-week pilot, see costs and quality on our financial summarization use case, also need spanish support for LATAM customers.
[00:28] Maya: perfect. can you walk through your current stack and constraints? like are you running anything on-prem now, and what's the plan if we go dedicated?
[00:36] Ravi: currently inference is on GCP managed endpoints for smaller tasks. production ACLs are in a shared project. main constraints: strict latency for live chat summaries < 500ms p50 ideally, and token cost is a big factor — we process a lot of docs. security: we need VPC peering or private link, and our compliance team requires SOC2 audit evidence and KMS integration.
[00:58] Sara: also retention rules — raw user inputs cannot be stored outside our control; so for hosted we need a private deployment or guaranteed no retention.
[01:08] Luis: got it. Redwood Dedicated or Private can address isolation, Dedicated with reserved capacity supports VPC + KMS. for a POC we often run on hosted with strict data handling controls or on a short-lived private deployment depending on the security gating.
[01:26] Ravi: POC objective: make sure model quality meets our extractive/abstractive summarization baseline for earnings calls and customer support tickets, plus bilingual spanish accuracy. success criteria would be: 1) summary ROUGE/LU paraphrase thresholds vs our golden set, 2) < 5% hallucination rate on a held-out set, 3) latency p50 < 500ms for single-turn summaries at our target token lengths, and 4) cost per 1k tokens under our threshold.
[01:55] Maya: excellent — that's granular and helpful. for model shortlist, we've had success recommending a mix of quantized open models for cost and a higher-quality fp16 variant for quality checks. thinking about models: Llama 3 family (if available open weights), Mistral 7B-v0.2-ish, and Meta's open variants, maybe Gemma, but avoid inconsistency — also include Open-weights instruction-tuned models like Mixtral and RedPine-7B (note: some names may vary).
[02:25] Ravi: are we considering Llama 3? licensing is sticky — we prefer fully open permissive LMs. also quality-wise, we've seen big gaps between 7B and 13B+ models for finance jargon.
[02:38] Luis: yes licensing matters — we'll prioritize models with usable weights for commercial POCs. shortlist candidate list I propose: - Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized), - RedPine-13B (13B instr-tuned), - Mixtral-8x7B ensemble (if available), - MPT-30B-instruct (if they can be run), and a smaller distilled model for latency tests. we'll include an off-the-shelf open instruction-tuned 13B as the baseline for quality/cost comparisons.
[03:05] Sara: can you run Spanish evals on these models out of the box or need extra finetune?
[03:10] Luis: out-of-the-box some models have decent multilingual support, but specialized finance jargon in Spanish will need prompt engineering and likely a small adapter / LoRA or retrieval augmentation to hit your accuracy bars. for the POC we recommend retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with your internal docs to reduce hallucination.
[03:28] Tom: what's the bandwidth for benchmarks — how many samples and what metrics do you need?
[03:33] Maya: we'll ask for a representative 200-500 example set for the POC — split across long/short docs and languages. metrics: latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, ROUGE / BLEU or embedding-semantic-similarity for paraphrase, and a manual hallucination check on a 50-sample slice. Luis will provide a benchmark template.
[03:52] Ravi: timeline idea: week 0 — confirm dataset + success criteria, week 1 — Redwood runs onboarding and baseline runs, week 2 — tuning (prompt, quantization), week 3 — final benchmark + report. customer then decides. can we get a dedicated run for worst-case latency tests?
[04:10] Luis: yes we can simulate concurrency and throughput profiles. need your target QPS and average tokens per request.
[04:16] Sara: our peak is about 10 QPS with 3 concurrent workers, average request is 450 tokens in and 200 tokens out. monthly active is ~5M tokens.
[04:26] Luis: that helps. for Dedicated you'd reserve a pool sized for steady-state throughput; for the POC we can provision a temporary dedicated cluster to stress test, or run hosted with throttling.
[04:38] Ravi: about quantization — does Redwood support 4-bit / q4_k_m or INT8-like for these models? we care about throughput gains.
[04:45] Luis: yes runtime supports q4 and 8-bit variants for many open models, plus kernel selection for attention that reduces latency. we'll include both fp16 and q4 tests; for bookkeeping we'll log perplexity-ish and output-quality metrics since quantization sometimes regresses hallucination behavior.
[05:03] Maya: any red flags from security / procurement perspective?
[05:07] Tom: procurement will want an estimate first — EULA terms matter, and if we run a private deploy there's a separate license. our legal is sensitive to models that have unclear commercial rights.
[05:18] Maya: we'll flag explicitly which model weights meet your licensing bar. we can also run a small on-prem evaluation if needed.
[05:25] Ravi: how do you handle data residency? some LATAM data must stay in-region.
[05:29] Luis: Redwood can route requests by region, and Private deployments can be provisioned in a customer VPC in the region. for hosted, we can restrict processing to a region if region is available. we'll capture data flow in the architecture doc.
[05:43] Sara: about hallucination checks, can we plug our classifier to auto-detect hallucinated entities?
[05:48] Luis: yes, we can pipeline outputs through your classifier as a post-process; better yet, RAG with strong retrieval reduces hallucination. we'll prototype without fine-tuning first, then test a small LoRA if needed.
[06:02] Maya: ok let's shape the POC success criteria into measurable thresholds. I'll repeat: (1) ROUGE-L >= 0.48 vs golden on English summaries, (2) Spanish parity +/- 5% relative to English, (3) hallucination rate < 5%, (4) p50 latency < 500ms at 1-3 concurrency, (5) cost < $X per 1k tokens — we'll put a range in the proposal. does that sound right?
[06:26] Ravi: yes that maps. we'll get the golden set ready and share by Friday.
[06:31] Tom: commercial ask — what's rough cost delta between fp16 13B and q4 13B? we need order-of-magnitude for runway.
[06:39] Luis: rough thumb: q4 can be 2-4x throughput improvement and 2-3x cost reduction vs fp16 depending on kernel and batch. but quality may drop a notch; we need to show concrete metrics in the benchmark.
[06:52] Ravi: competitors — we've tested OpenAI's API for quality baseline; it is strong but costs are higher and we want model control. Anthropic was okay on safety but lacking Spanish in some tests. Cohere was fast but hallucinated more on finance facts.
[07:08] Maya: noted. for the POC model shortlist we'll include 3 tiers: small low-latency model (Mistral-7B quantized), mid-tier 13B open variant for cost/quality balance, and a high-quality 30B-ish reference if licensing allows. we'll also include a retrieval-augmented baseline using your docs.
[07:26] Sara: how long to stand up the private deployment if we need it?
[07:30] Luis: private deployment typically takes 2-3 weeks for infra and certs; for a POC we recommend hosted with strict controls unless procurement insists on private. Dedicated with reserved capacity can be 1-2 weeks for reserved infra.
[07:44] Ravi: for the benchmarks, what about hallucination scoring — do you do automatic checks or manual?
[07:49] Luis: both. automatic heuristics for entity hallucination + sampling for manual review. we'll include a manual audit of 50 samples and flag hallucinations with rationale.
[07:58] Maya: ok let's cover telemetry: Redwood Console will give you per-route latency, token breakdown, and cost. we can hook traces to your APM.
[08:06] Tom: any particular prompt templates that work for legal/finance summarization?
[08:10] Luis: we have templates tuned for earnings calls — explicit instructions, output format constraints, and structured fields (key metrics, entities, sentiment). we'll share examples.
[08:19] Ravi: bilingual — will we need separate prompts per language or unified pipeline?
[08:23] Luis: you can do unified if the model supports multilingual; often better to detect language and apply language-specific prefixes and retrieval. retrieval corpus should include language-tagged docs.
[08:33] Sara: data requirements — we'll anonymize PII. is that fine for the benchmark?
[08:37] Maya: yes, anonymized data is preferred. for encryption at rest we support KMS integrations.
[08:42] Ravi: sample size — we're good with 300 examples (200 en, 100 es) for initial run.
[08:48] Luis: great. we'll design bench to run each model at 3 concurrency levels and both fp16 and q4 variants where supported.
[08:57] Maya: what about fallback policies — if late night spikes cause latency breaches how does Redwood degrade gracefully?
[09:03] Luis: Redwood can route to cheaper model variants or a cached summary if available; also can throttle or shed non-critical requests. we'll document fallback SLOs.
[09:13] Tom: procurement will need the security pack and SOC2 docs.
[09:16] Maya: I'll attach our SOC2 report and the private deployment checklist.
[09:20] Ravi: any concerns about model licensing for Llama family?
[09:23] Luis: depends on the release — we'll only include weights that are clear for commercial use; our legal team will annotate each candidate.
[09:30] Sara: OK — can you also include model size vs memory footprint and expected GPU type for the dedicated pool?
[09:36] Luis: yes, we'll provide mapping: 13B ~ A10G or equivalent in fp16 with X batch, q4 can run on smaller GPUs. details in the benchmark doc.
[09:44] Maya: recap and next steps: Maya to send formal POC proposal with pricing, Luis to share benchmark template and model shortlist with licensing notes, Aureus to send golden dataset and success criteria doc. target dates: proposal by 2026-12-18, benchmark ready-to-run by 2026-12-21.
[09:58] Ravi: agreed, we'll prioritize the dataset.
[10:01] Tom: schedule a follow-up tech call during the benchmark week.
[10:05] Maya: yeah let's set a 30-min check-in for 2026-12-22 to go over early results.
[10:11] Meeting close, thanks everyone.
